prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title: 'Scabies: break the household cycle'. Two side-by-side visual networks, each four simple friendly human bust silhouettes arranged around an open circle. No facial or skin pathology; no mites or anatomical detail. Left network: only the bottom-left person has a teal treatment check. Coral curved arrows form a complete clockwise loop among all four icons. Label above 'Only one person treated'; short label in centre 'Reinfestation can continue'. Right network: all four people each carry the identical teal check. Use pale dashed curved former-contact paths with clear gaps rather than a complete loop; put a large open broken-circle symbol at centre. Label above 'Treat close contacts together'; centre 'Break the cycle'. A small folded-laundry icon at bottom accompanies the one short reminder 'Clean used clothing and bedding'. Balanced warm paper; the loops and check coverage must make the comparison evident without prose boxes.

teaching.question: Why are household members treated together when someone has scabies?
teaching.answer: Untreated close contacts can perpetuate transmission and reinfestation. Simultaneous treatment, together with appropriate cleaning of used clothing and bedding, helps break the cycle.

title: Breaking the household scabies cycle
caption: Treating the affected person and all household members and close contacts at the same time helps prevent scabies reinfestation.
alt: Two household networks contrast treatment of one person with simultaneous treatment of all close contacts, breaking the reinfestation loop.

review.notes: Compared full pixels against specification: both networks have four people; left has one treatment check and a complete clockwise loop; right has four checks and visibly interrupted paths plus a broken ring. No internal anatomy or skin pathology. Cleaning reminder matches CDC. Simultaneous treatment coverage is the clear visual distinction.
